creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Top finding of the clig.dev conformance audit filed 2026-07-14. Neither layer suggests corrections:

- `rad chek` gives a bare "Unknown file or command"
- `--frmat` gives a bare "unknown flag" from `ra`

Both pieces already exist: `core/fuzzy.go` holds Levenshtein machinery, and `ra` exposes `ParseHooks.ErrorHint`. Script-level identifiers already get did-you-mean; the CLI surface doesn't.

Second finding from the same card, cheap and adjacent: global flags only parse after the script path, so `rad --color never script.rad` fails.

---

### Orientation

This is three small independent changes in two different layers. They can ship separately.

- **`rad chek`** - the "Unknown file or command" error is Rad's own, at `core/runner.go:146`, the last line of `detectInvocationType`. The candidate set is right there: `core.CmdsByName`, built in `core/cmds.go:42-56` from eight embedded commands (`new`, `docs`, `check`, `fmt`, `home`, `gen-id`, `stash`, `explain`).
- **`--frmat`** - the "unknown flag" error comes from `ra`, not from Rad (`ra_cmd_parse.go:624` in the module cache: `fmt.Errorf("unknown flag: --%s", flagName)`). Rad already has a hook into ra's error path.
- **Global flags before the script path** - `core/runner.go:116-120`. Any first arg starting with `-` short-circuits to `NoScript`, so `rad --color never script.rad` never finds the script. There is already a `todo` on line 117 flagging the adjacent `rad -- myscript` case.

### Watch out for

ra's unknown-flag error is a bare `fmt.Errorf`, not a typed error, so `errors.As` cannot reach it the way `*ra.TooManyPositionalArgsError` can. String-matching ra's message from Rad is exactly the "workaround filed in the wrong repo" that `AGENTS.md` warns about. `ra` is first-party (`go.mod:12` pins `v0.8.1`, checkout at `~/src/ra`): add a typed `UnknownFlagError` upstream, iterate with a local `replace` directive, and remove the directive before committing. Tagging and releasing `ra` is the maintainer's call, so flag that this half cannot fully land without a release.

ra also already knows the full flag set at the point of failure, which makes "should the suggestion live in ra instead of Rad?" a real question worth asking before writing code in Rad.
title: Add did-you-mean for CLI typos
